Lord Canning, at Allahabad, announced Queen Victoria's proclamation to "the Princes, Chiefs and Peoples of India." The Queen's proclamation, known as the Magna Carta of the Indian people, disclaimed territorial extensions, promised religious toleration, guaranteed the rights of Indian princes, and pledged equal treatment to Indians and Europeans. The proclamation declared that: • Those who laid down arms by 2 January 1859 would be pardoned, except those directly involved in the murder of British subjects • Official service would be open to all • Due regard would be given to the ancient usages and customs of India. • It transferred the power to govern India from the East India Company to the British Crown and declared Queen Victoria as the sovereign of British India. Provisions of the Act are mentioned below – The company’s territories in India were to be governed by Queen, the company ceased to exercise its power and control over these territories. India was now to be governed in the name of the Queen. The Queen’s principal secretary of state for India received the powers and duties of the company’s court of directors. A council of fifteen members was appointed to assist the secretary of state for India. The Council became an advisory body for Indian affairs. For all communications between Britain and India, the secretary of the state became the real channel. The Crown was empowered to appoint a Governor-General and the Governors of the Presidencies. An Indian Civil Service was to be created under the control of the secretary of state. All the property and other assets of the East India Company were transferred to the crown. The crown also assumed the responsibilities of the company along with their related treaties, contracts and so forth.

Who among the following did not rebel against the British East India Company’s control over them?

s:
Assertion (A): Andhra region was not greatly affected by the Revolt of 1857 as Andhra had no local leaders.
Reason (R): The then reigning Nizam, Nawab Afzal-ud-Dowla adopted a pro-British attitude.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
x:
Assertion (A) is false. It is incorrect to state that the Andhra region remained unaffected by the Revolt of 1857 because there were no local leaders. Although the revolt did not assume the same intensity as in North India, several local revolts and anti-British activities occurred in Andhra and the Hyderabad State. Leaders such as Turrebaz Khan in Hyderabad actively resisted the British, and anti-British sentiment was visible in different parts of the Telugu-speaking region. Therefore, the absence of local leaders was not the reason for the limited impact of the revolt.
Reason (R) is true. The Nizam of Hyderabad, Afzal-ud-Dowla (Asaf Jah V), remained loyal to the British during the Revolt of 1857. His cooperation helped the British suppress revolutionary activities in the Deccan and prevented the uprising from spreading widely in the Hyderabad State. The loyalty of the Nizam was one of the important reasons for the failure of the revolt in the Deccan. Since the Assertion is false and the Reason is true, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Nizam during 1857 – Afzal-ud-Dowla
• Hyderabad Resident – Played a key role in suppressing the revolt.
• Turrebaz Khan – Prominent freedom fighter of Hyderabad during the Revolt of 1857.

s: Year of the Rampa Revolution?
x:
The Rampa Rebellion of 1879 was an important tribal uprising in the Godavari Agency against British rule. The rebellion was mainly caused by the Madras Forest Act, restrictions on shifting cultivation, heavy taxation and interference in tribal customs. It was one of the earliest tribal revolts in Andhra before the famous Alluri Sitarama Raju-led Rampa Rebellion (1922–24). Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:
• First Rampa Rebellion – 1879
• Later Rampa Rebellion – 1922–24 (Alluri Sitarama Raju)

s: Who had led the Rampa rebellion?
x: Alluri Sitarama Raju led the 1922-24 Rampa rebellion among the Koya and Konda Dora tribes. Velu Thampi was Travancore's Diwan, and the 1879 Rampa rising was led by Tammandora, so the other options are wrong.

s: A direct battle between the British and the followers of Alluri Sitarama Raju took place at?
x:
The famous Battle of Panjerighat witnessed a direct confrontation between the British forces and the followers of Alluri Sitarama Raju during the Rampa Rebellion (1922–24). The battle demonstrated the courage and military skill of the tribal revolutionaries who resisted British rule in the Agency areas. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Direct Battle – Panjerighat
• Leader – Alluri Sitarama Raju
